context: Tests whether the agent correctly maps a set of team requirements to Tessl primitives (skill, rule, MCP server, hooks), justifies each choice, avoids padding with unneeded primitives, and correctly handles a not-GA primitive (hooks) by deferring rather than planning to ship it.

checklist.name: Skill for PR review
checklist.description: Recommends a skill (not a rule or command) for the task-specific, on-demand PR review workflow

checklist.name: Rule for import convention
checklist.description: Recommends a rule (not a skill) for the always-on Python import ordering convention

checklist.name: MCP server for metrics API
checklist.description: Recommends an MCP server (not a skill or rule) for the live metrics API query capability

checklist.name: Hooks deferred, not shipped
checklist.description: Does NOT plan to ship hooks for the commit-triggered summaries; notes that hooks are not GA or unavailable, and defers the requirement as a follow-up

checklist.name: Justification for each primitive
checklist.description: Provides a brief justification for each primitive choice (not just a list of types), explaining why that primitive fits the requirement

checklist.name: No padding
checklist.description: Does NOT add extra primitives (e.g. a command, a second MCP server, additional rules/skills) that were not needed by the stated requirements

checklist.name: Plan is concise
checklist.description: The composition-plan.md is structured as a short plan (not a full implementation or lengthy spec) — a few lines per component rather than detailed code or exhaustive prose

checklist.name: Plugin shape stated
checklist.description: States the overall proposed shape — whether this is a single skill or a plugin — and names which primitives will be bundled together

checklist.name: No secrets hard-coded for MCP
checklist.description: Does not hard-code the bearer token or API URL secret in the plan; notes that credentials should be provided via environment variable or configuration

checklist.name: Skill vs rule distinction clear
checklist.description: The plan explicitly distinguishes between always-on (rule) and on-demand/task-specific (skill) as the reason for the primitive split, not just listing names
